$comment: Pre-registration of the code-awareness measurement (#579, #588, epic #572; C-089..C-094). Version 2 replaces version 1 (git history, commit before this one): v1 asked 'where is symbol X' and measured search tokens; its only clean run used a find_code payload that no longer exists and was withdrawn (BEFUND.md, 69da488). v2 asks the question the feature is built for — 'what breaks if I change this' — with the design from the Codex counter-review of PR #582 and thresholds decided by the product owner. Fixed BEFORE any v2 scenario has been run. Amending anything after a run has started invalidates that run: bump registration_version and say which version a report belongs to.
registered_by: Claude Opus 5; thresholds decided by Daniel Nevoigt on 2026-09-18
$comment_status: The thresholds below are product-owner decisions (2026-09-18), not proposals. A report against them may say pass or fail.
question: When an agent is told a concrete planned change to one file, does code awareness (find_code) make it name more of the files that the change actually breaks, without naming more wrong files and without costing disproportionate context?
$comment_question: One question. The unit is a CHANGE, not a symbol: v1's 34 symbols came from 12 files and were not 34 independent tasks.

unit.name: historical_change
unit.definition: One file F changed in one historical commit C of this repository on main. The scenario is set on C's parent: the agent is shown F's diff from C as the planned change and asked which OTHER files would stop compiling because of it.
unit.independence: At most one scenario per file, at most three per directory. The bootstrap resamples directories, not scenarios, so scenarios sharing a directory are not counted as independent evidence.
unit.$comment_independence: Strictly one per directory would leave too few candidates in flat directories like packages/daemon/src; the cap plus the clustered bootstrap is the honest middle.

ground_truth.definition: On a worktree at C's parent, typecheck every workspace package (src and __tests__) before and after applying ONLY F's diff from C. A file is affected when it carries at least one type error after the mutation that it did not carry before. F itself is excluded.
ground_truth.adjudication: Each truth set is reviewed by hand before any arm runs; a file is removed only with a written reason (e.g. the error is an artefact of applying one file of a multi-file commit in isolation), and additions are not made by hand.
ground_truth.$comment: The graph is never used as truth, and co-change alone is not truth: files changed together are not necessarily files that break. Limitation, stated up front: this truth is type-level. Behavioural breakage that only a test run would show is not in it.

scenario_inclusion.commit_range: main, non-merge commits, oldest first up to the frozen range end recorded in the scenario file
scenario_inclusion.file_filter: F is a .ts file under packages/*/src/, not a test
scenario_inclusion.must_break_something: the truth set has at least one file
scenario_inclusion.$comment_max: A change that breaks more than 40 files is a mechanical rename, not a question of judgement; it would dominate every mean.

primary_metric.name: affected_file_recall
primary_metric.definition: Per scenario: |named ∩ truth| / |truth|, where `named` is the file list in the agent's final answer, normalized to repo-relative POSIX paths.

secondary_metrics.name: affected_file_precision
secondary_metrics.definition: |named ∩ truth| / |named|; 1 when nothing is named and truth is empty (never the case by inclusion).

secondary_metrics.name: context_chars
secondary_metrics.definition: Characters of all tool results the agent received in the scenario (the context it spent searching), reported as tokens at 4 chars per token.

secondary_metrics.name: dependents_block_followed_by_edit
secondary_metrics.source: real-session telemetry (`bastra logs --stats`, line `followed`), not the scenario run
secondary_metrics.$comment: The block fires on edits and the scenario agent does not edit, so this is measured in daily use (#588).

treatment.name: code awareness on
treatment.description: Headless Claude Code with exactly one MCP tool, find_code, answering from a graph built by the pinned Graphify on the scenario's worktree. Same text search tools as control.

control.name: no-graph control arm
control.description: The same headless Claude Code with no MCP server at all: text search and file reads only.

arms.isolation: Both arms: `--setting-sources project --strict-mcp-config --no-session-persistence`, a fresh process per scenario and arm, cwd a throwaway worktree outside the repository. Verified 2026-09-18: no user hooks, no user CLAUDE.md, no Recall tools reach the agent.
arms.tools: Read and read-only shell search (grep, rg, git grep, find, ls, cat, sed, head); no edits, no subagents, no web.

design.paired_on: the same scenario run through both arms
design.arm_order: randomized per scenario by a seeded shuffle; seed recorded in the scenario file before the first run

sample.$comment: 30 independent changes. If fewer qualify in the commit range, the report says `underpowered` (18.1) instead of a verdict.

thresholds.$comment: Decided by Daniel Nevoigt, 2026-09-18. All must hold for a pass.
thresholds.$comment_recall: Mean paired difference treatment - control in affected_file_recall of at least 10 percentage points, AND the lower bound of its 95 % bootstrap interval above 0.
thresholds.$comment_precision: Mean paired difference in precision not below -0.05: more hits bought with more wrong files do not count.
thresholds.$comment_context: On scenarios solved in BOTH arms (solved = recall >= 0.8), median treatment context_chars at most 1.25 x median control. Cost is compared only where both got the answer, so a cheap wrong answer cannot win.

latency_non_regression.source: lane telemetry with code awareness on vs off

hook_block_keep.gating_for: the automatic dependents block only, not find_code
hook_block_keep.$comment: After at least 50 blocks in real sessions, at least 15 % must be followed by an edit to a file they named in the same session; otherwise the block goes off by default and find_code stays.

statistics.method: paired bootstrap, 10 000 resamples, resampling directories (clusters) with replacement

$comment_failure: A missed threshold is recorded as the finding; thresholds are not moved afterwards.

run_conditions.per_scenario_base: C's parent SHA, recorded in the scenario file with the graph's sha256

contents: scenario file with base SHAs and seed
raw stream-json transcript of every arm run
archive.$comment: v1 checked in only aggregates; the raw logs were gone. Everything needed to re-score is kept.

graphify_benchmark_7_3x.$comment: Graphify reports 7.3x fewer tokens in its own benchmark. Per 24 and C-029, no external target value is a Bastra gate.

reporting_duties: The primary metric per scenario and as the paired mean with its 95 % interval.
Precision and context as above, with the per-scenario rows.
The latency comparison with p50 and p90.
The hook-block followed share with its N, or `not yet 50 blocks`.
The registration_version this report belongs to.
An honest status (`underpowered` / `not_evaluable` per 18.1) where the sample does not support a verdict.
